cells.place: Hony. General Secretary, A.H.R. Society, Rajahmundry.
cells.remarks: Records the grant by Manujēndra, son of king Dēvēndravarman, of some lands in the Nīlaka-grāma situated in the Vārāhakavarttani-vishaya (district) and Chintachēḍu-grāma in Hōmva-vishaya, in favour of Kauṇḍuka-Guṇḍēśvara. The gift was received by Sāmavēda-bhaṭṭa, son of Bhāgavadatta of Vārāhakavarttani-vishaya and (of) Chaḷḷakōṇḍa. The writer of the document was Chidāpa, son of Kāyastha Khaḍama. An endorsement registers the grant of the two localities called Yēgū or Ēgu and Mahanta, collectedly known as Gūṇḍi and situated in Koṇḍaguḍi, in favour of Yōgīśman by king Dēvēndravarman. Published in JAHRS, Vol. XX, pp. 161-70; Ep. Ind., Vol. XXI, 177ff.

cells.place: Deputy Commissioner of Commercial Taxes, Guntur. Narsannapeta Taluk, Srikakulam Dist. †
cells.remarks: Leased from Siṁhāpura. Records that Mahārāja Śatrudamana, a devotee of Dāmodaravāsavina, granted three hamlets called Puha-grāma, Vasuvātaka and Gō-vāṭaka in the agrahāra of Giri-Kalinga-Varddhamāna, to Sarvadarman and Vappaśar-mman, who were sons of Yajñadatta, of the Kāśyapa-gōtra, 68th and the Taittirīya-śākhā, and to the village residents of Pathuva-grāma. Vaidya Kṛishṇadatta was the dūta or executor of the grant. In characters of about the 5th century A.D. Published in Bhārat, March, 1955, pp. 86 ff.; Ep. Ind., Vol. XXXI, pp. 80 ff.

cells.remarks: Issued from Matrchandana-vātaka. Records the grant of some land to the Brāhmaṇa Durgadatta belonging to the Kōngōda-mandala to the Brāhmaṇa Gōtasvāmin of the Jatūkarnya gotra having the Vasiśhtha, Ātrēya and Jātūkarnya pravaras and of the Vājasaneya charaṇa and Kānva śākhā. Mahāsāmanta Prabhañjanēva witnessed the document and approved, and the writer of the document, Sthāviravichchhedamrań, and the Dūta Pēfāpāla Balavarman sealed it. cells.date: V. S. 1192, Chaitra va. 5, Tuesday, Vis- hu-saṅkrānti=1136 A.D., March 24.
cells.remarks: Records a grant of 24 padas of land in Vakshatapadashṭaka in Valhaṇḍā-grāma in Mahisēṁha-vishaya to Sōmēśarman of the Mōdha-gōtra. The king was camping at Pātāḷīputra. The king made the grant while camping at Parēyi-grāma. Records in addition that four padas of land were granted by the king to Dīkshita Nārāyaṇa of Gautama-gōtra, who was earlier a resident of Kōśala-dēśa. The land was granted in exchange for some other specified lands which he had received from Nāduka, the priest of Rājñī Lakhamadēvī, and Sōmēka. 14 padas of land were granted to Sahajśarman, brother of Sōmēśarman, who was also a resident of Kōśala-dēśa. The grant was made by Chāṇḍaladēvī in exchange for his lands at Pāpalā-grāma. The document was written by the Dharmalēkhin Sadha of Vāstavya-vaṁśa and engraved by the Vijñānin Ūhēna belong- ing to the Rītika community. Published in Ep. Ind., XXII, pp. 119 ff.

cells.location: Sultanpur, Rajshahi Dist.
cells.place: Varendra Research Society, Rajshahi.
cells.remarks: Records an endowment of 9 kulyavāpas of land by the artisan Bhima and others with the permission of Achyutadāsa, the Āyuktaka in charge of the Śṛṅgavēra vīthī, and also of the local adhikaraṇa and the leading men and house-holders of the village in favour of the temple of the goddess Bhaṭṭārikā-Mahādēvī, i.e., Mahāsaṁdatta, who belonged to Puṇḍravardhana and were students of the Vājasanēya school in order to enable them to perform the five great sacrifices (pañcha-mahāyajña) uninter- ruptedly. In characters of the 5th century A.D. Published in IHQ. Vol. XIX, pp. 12 ff.; Ep. Ind., Vol. XXXI, pp. 57 ff.

cells.location: Asutosh Museum
cells.place: Stone tablet containing inset figure of Gaṇeśa (on the front and a side of the tablet). Findspot: Bhubaneswar, Orissa.
cells.date: Year 22, Kārtika ba. 7, Sunday= 1396 A.D., Septem- ber 4.
cells.language: Tamil and Oriyā, Tamil and Gauḍiya.
cells.remarks: Refers to the gift of 12 vāṭis of land at Vāghamāra or Vāgha- marā to Tpora-mahā-uni, the head of the Siddhēśvara- naṭha, at Krilavāśa-kshētra, as an Ekaśālā brahma-bhikshā for the longer maintenance of the daily feeding of ascetics. The donor, mahāmaṇi mortgaged the land for 150 gold Mādhas to Durgābhāṭṭa-āchārya and further borrowed 10 Mādhas and 30 Pauśis of paddy from the latter's father-in-law Uttarēśvara- nāyaka over and above the sum of three hundred pātīs as the exact pontiff of the Maṭha, and Durgābhāṭṭa were friends, the latter released the land, for the longevity of the reigning monarch, to enable Tapaschakravartin to continue the bhikshā for the sustenance of the ascetics living, from Chhu-di- piva-dēśa and Kāñchī-dēśa. Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. XXXII, pp. 229 ff.

cells.place:
Hero stone lying near the library
building.
cells.date:
Śaka 963, Vikrama,
Chaitra ba. 14,
Friday. Irregular.
cells.remarks: States that Chandana, commander of the elephant force, attacked the elephant corps of Bhoja, and having killed several men established his own camp. While he was encamped there, an encounter between Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Kēsārarasa and Mahalika Bhōja. The encounter is said to have taken place when Tribhuvanamalla (i.e. Vikramāditya VI) was returning from a victorious campaign in the south-west, having quarters, burnt the city of Dhārā and planted a pillar of victory.

cells.date: ... M a ṛ g a ś ī r a, amāvāsyā, Monday.
